name: WA-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Deep-blue D+39 Seattle-area district held by a Democratic incumbent
Jayapal's roughly $2.85M raised and $1.77M on hand versus about $12K for Sheth
Prediction markets price Jayapal at roughly 98% to win
No public polling or expert ratings, but fundamentals leave the challenger no visible path
model.rationale: A D+39 district, an entrenched incumbent with a fundraising advantage of more than 200-to-1, and a market price near 98% all point the same direction. With no polling or ratings suggesting competition, this stays safely Democratic with an expected margin in the mid-30s.
model.watch: Only a dramatic late-breaking development or an unexpected national wave toward Republicans could narrow the margin, and nothing in the evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's 7th District, anchored in Seattle, is among the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+39. Incumbent Democrat Pramila Jayapal advanced to the general election against Republican Nirav Sheth, a first-time challenger with minimal resources. Jayapal has raised about $2.85 million and holds $1.77 million on hand, while Sheth has raised roughly $12,000, leaving him little ability to introduce himself to voters.

No public polling covers the race and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the lopsided money picture. Prediction markets give Jayapal roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. The evidence points to a comfortable Democratic victory; the realistic question is the size of the margin, not which party carries the seat.
